_comment: Matches the REAL existing 'UK' tab column layout in your tracker exactly. UNIFIED 2026-08-14 to match USA's standard column order/keys, per explicit instruction ('same the UK, poland tab as USA... Follow the USA tab as standard one'). Two deliberate, user-approved exceptions to a literal 1:1 match with USA (confirmed via AskUserQuestion before this ran): (1) UK keeps its own 'VAT' column -- real non-zero historical tax amounts (e.g. 53 to 50000 across its 13 real rows) that a strict USA-only column set would have deleted; placed right after Total Amount, same as before. (2) USA's 'State' and UK's 'Country' are different concepts (US state vs client's own country) that just happen to sit in the same column position (3) -- kept as their own tab-specific header/key rather than merged into one. Physically restructured on the real device file 2026-08-14 via scripts/surgical_unify_uk_poland.py (raw-XML surgical patch -- every other sheet, including India, verified byte-for-byte untouched; backup saved alongside the real file as 'Invoice Traker_BACKUP_2026-08-14_pre-uk-poland-unify.xlsx').
_two_phase_flow_note: 'Invoice Description' / 'Client Mail To' / 'INT CC Mail' used to be TRAILING columns (added after-the-fact, 2026-08-1x, for the two-phase flow) -- moved 2026-08-14 to sit right after Company Name, matching where USA already has them.
_mis_verified_note: 'MIS Verified' (2026-08-12) is set by the real MIS project-info API call made right when the row is appended (see src/mis/mis_api.py) -- True only if that call actually succeeded for the row's PF ID; False (never blocks the append) if the API failed, timed out, or the token was expired, so accounts knows to check that project ID by hand.
_currency_note: 'Currency' (2026-08-13) -- every new row gets this tab's 'default_currency' (GBP) below unless the CP email's own 'Currency' row says otherwise (parse_invoice_summary.py normalizes it to a 3-letter code).
_department_received_amount_note: 'Department' and 'Received amount' added 2026-08-14 as part of the USA-layout unification -- USA already had both (always blank in practice, filled in by hand if at all); UK never had either before. Historical UK rows are blank in both, same policy as every other trailing/inserted column added so far.
